subject: Renewal paperwork: term swap, seat split, and orderbook sequencing
messages:

Cc: procurement@cloudhaven.com
Date: Tue, 05 Dec 2028 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Renewal & expansion — term change + capacity bump (Cloudhaven DH-2028-0472)

Jordan —

Thanks for the quick sync last week. Attached is a short summary of what procurement and our engineering leads are asking for as we approach the renewal window. High level: we want to move from the current 12-month term to a 24-month term, split the seat allocation across two legal entities (Cloudhaven Core / Cloudhaven EU), and increase inference capacity roughly 3x for Q1 on the Dedicated pool.

A few specific asks so we can prepare an internal PO:
- Confirm whether Redwood can split the order into two orderforms under the same MSA (one for Core, one for EU) while preserving a single negotiated discount.
- Clarify billing proration if the new term starts mid-quarter (we may start the replacement on 2029-01-15).
- We need a clear path for capacity ramp and a cap on burst costs for the first 90 days.
- Data residency: our security team wants explicit EU data residency language for the EU orderform.

I've attached our renewal request doc and a draft PO (procurement will issue the formal PO once terms are agreed). Can you confirm process and next steps? We want to run this through legal and procurement this month.

Thanks,
Sam
Sam Taylor
Head of Platform Engineering | Cloudhaven
attachments: Cloudhaven_Renewal_Request.pdf, CH_PO_notes.txt

Subject: Re: Renewal & expansion — term change + capacity bump (Cloudhaven DH-2028-0472)

Sam — thanks for laying this out. Appreciate the clear asks. High-level yes: we can support separate orderforms under the same MSA and carry one negotiated discount across both, but legal will want a brief amendment to the MSA to call out the split and the EU residency carveout.

Proposed path (suggested):
1) Legal: draft a short Term Amendment to the MSA that does three things — (a) switches base term to 24 months for the covered orderforms, (b) includes EU data residency carveout language for the EU orderform, and (c) defines prorated billing for mid-quarter starts.
2) Orderbook sequencing: create Orderform A (Cloudhaven Core — seats + baseline capacity) and Orderform B (Cloudhaven EU — seats + region-bound capacity). We can attach a signed mutual action plan to sequence activation dates.
3) Capacity & surge: run a 90-day ramp schedule in the MAP and add a surge-cost cap (Ben — can you propose the pricing cap options?).
4) Sign path: legal approves redline, procurement issues PO, then DocuSign for orderforms + amendment.

Looping in Kimberly for redlines and Ben for pricing. Marissa — please note CS will own activation and staging, we need runbook for staggered rollouts.

Attaching an internal one-pager with the above plan (jordan_proposal_v1.docx). If that looks ok I can ask legal to start an MSA redline and share it with your counsel for parallel review.

Thanks,
Jordan
Jordan Blake
Enterprise Account Executive | Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Renewal & expansion — term change + capacity bump (Cloudhaven DH-2028-0472)

Jordan / Sam — I've reviewed Jordan's proposal and drafted initial redlines. Key legal considerations below; redline attached (MSA_redline_cloudhaven_20281205.docx).

1) Term language: switch to a 24-month primary term is OK, but we recommend limiting automatic renewals to 12-month rolling periods after the initial 24 months — this preserves some flexibility if there are material changes to capacity or residency obligations.

2) Orderform split: acceptable to have separate Orderforms under one MSA, but we need a short schedule that lists the orderform IDs and the discount reference to avoid ambiguity. I added an Exhibit listing Orderform A/B IDs.

3) Data residency: added explicit data residency clause for the Cloudhaven EU orderform requiring that EU-submitted inference requests and logs be routed to EU-region Dedicated pools and that KMS keys for that orderform be EU-resident. This will require ops confirmation that the private deployment option is respected.

4) Billing & proration: inserted clear proration formula for mid-quarter activations (pro rata by day, with first invoice showing prorated baseline and estimated surge reserve). We also added a reconciliation invoice at the end of the first month of activation.

5) Surge costs & caps: we can agree to a 90-day ramp with a negotiated cap on overage rates. Legal wants language that caps discretionary surges to a max percent above baseline and preserves Redwood's right to throttle if safety or capacity constraints occur.

6) Indemnity & liability: reduced exposure by narrowing the indemnity trigger to willful misconduct and gross negligence for the new orderforms; added carveouts for customer-managed keys.

Marissa — I left a note where we should define rollback/rollback-trigger operationally (e.g., sustained latency > X ms for N minutes). Ops input required.

Sam — if this direction is acceptable I'll finalize the redline and send a clean amendment + orderform templates for procurement review.

Thanks,
Kimberly Park
Senior Counsel, Contracts | Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Renewal & expansion — term change + capacity bump (Cloudhaven DH-2028-0472)

Kimberly / Jordan — appreciate the quick turnaround and the redline. A few counterpoints from procurement and security after an internal review: they'd prefer uniform terms across legal entities (a single 24-month term for both Core and EU) to simplify the PO and amortization for our finance team.

On data residency: our security team is concerned about KMS key residency if Redwood's control plane remains in the US. They want either (a) customer-managed KMS in EU for the EU orderform, or (b) a contractual assurance that Redwood's control plane will not persist EU-region logs outside EU jurisdiction.

On surge cap: procurement proposed a hard cap at 20% above baseline for the first 90 days, with a reconciliation mechanism afterwards. We can live with a throttle clause for safety but want explicit cost protection.

Attached is the formal purchase order (CH_PO_472.pdf) — procurement will only issue the final PO once legal and pricing confirm. Happy to take a short call tomorrow if useful.

Best,
Sam

Thanks all — good alignment. Recap and next steps so procurement can surface the PO: 

Decisions to carry forward:
- Base approach: 24-month initial term covering both Orderform A (Cloudhaven Core) and Orderform B (Cloudhaven EU).
- Orderform split remains (two orderforms under one MSA) but discount and billing tied via an Exhibit that references both orderform IDs.
- Data residency: Kimberly will finalize language to allow customer-managed EU KMS for the EU orderform; if Cloudhaven provides EU KMS info we will include it in the Exhibit.
- Proration: pro rata by day for mid-quarter activations with a reconciliation invoice at month-end.
- Surge cap: initial agreement = 20% cap above baseline for first 90 days, with a post-90-day reconciliation and review period. Ben to confirm exact overage rates and present pricing options by EOD tomorrow.
- Rollback trigger / performance safety net: Marissa to propose a latency threshold and staged rollback plan by Friday.

Action items: 
- Kimberly: finalize redline + short Term Amendment and send clean PDFs for DocuSign (target: EOD 12/06).
- Ben: finalize pricing & surge-rate schedule (target: EOD 12/06).
- Marissa: draft activation runbook including rollback trigger (target: 12/08).
- Sam / Cloudhaven: confirm EU KMS details or confirm Redwood-managed alternative (target: 12/07).

Once Kimberly posts the clean amendment I'll send a DocuSign envelope that includes the Term Amendment + Orderform A/B templates + MAP. DocuSign link will be the single sign path for procurement. I attached the mutual action plan draft (mutual_action_plan_20281206.xlsx) which maps activation dates and responsibilities.

Sam — if that plan looks good I can kick the DocuSign today after Kimberly's clean files.

Thanks,
Jordan
